(b) Meadow Street east to Randolph Street: From Meadow Street east to Randolph Street and beyond, the Expressway will be built through the clearance and redevelopment area of the Randolph Project. The area north of the expressway will become a distributive commercial area, with a mixture of other nonresidential uses. No special treatment is proposed in the commercial area. The south side of the expressway between Meadow Street and Lombardy Street will be treated by acoustic shielding andd protective building arrangement or siting. Lombardy Street, which is at the same grade as the expressway, is proposed to be closed adjacent to the expressway. A 15-foot landscaped berm will be built from Allen Avenue across Lombardy Street to the Randolph Middle School. The Randolph School will become a Community Multi-Purpose Center. During the transition proposed changes should include acoustic shielding.
Randolph Street to the eastern Project Boundary:
This area is in the demolition and redevelopment area of the Project. As noted above the northern portion is planned for nonresidential use. The southern edge of the Expressway will consist of residential structures. These structures will be acoustically treated during construction and oriented so as to provide maximum noise protection, especially for sleeping quarters.
d. Expressway Lighting: Lighting for highways such as the proposed Downtown Expressway through the northerly portion of the Randolph Urban Renewal Area can be detrimental to adjoining areas unless the lighting facilities are specifically designed for compatibility with the surrounding area. To achieve compatibility, the amount of spill light onto the adjacent areas should be controlled to within acceptable limits and also the selected lighting equipment should present an essentially glare-free condition to the users of adjacent land as well as to users of the expressway.
In considering the impact of expressway lighting upon the urban renewal project, it should be recognized that definitive criteria regarding acceptable light levels for such projects have not yet been established.
